review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the simp lemmas about the idele coordinates and the idele norm. I looked at the uses of the unitEmbedding coordinate lemmas across the repo and at Mathlib's RingHom.toMonoidHom_eq_coe. The other simp lemmas (the ofAdicCompletion and ofCompletion coordinate lemmas, coe_ideleNorm_of*, ideleNorm_ideleNormSection) look consistent and don't compete. The one clear problem is the non-normal RHS of the two unitEmbedding coordinate lemmas. I have not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour beyond what the lemma statements imply.

findings.problem: Both @[simp] lemmas have an RHS built with `(algebraMap K _).toMonoidHom`. Mathlib's simp lemma `RingHom.toMonoidHom_eq_coe` rewrites `f.toMonoidHom` to the coercion `↑f`, and `MonoidHom.coe_ofClass` then rewrites that further. So the RHS is not in simp normal form, and simp has to normalise it again right after applying the lemma. The proofs in this file and elsewhere show this: `ideleNorm_unitEmbedding` follows the lemma with `Units.coe_map, RingHom.toMonoidHom_eq_coe, MonoidHom.coe_ofClass`. Congruence.lean does the same with `rw [ideleFiniteCoord_unitEmbedding, Units.coe_map]; simp only [MonoidHom.coe_ofClass, RingHom.toMonoidHom_eq_coe]`. The unit-valued form also means `simp` never reaches the coordinate in `K_v` directly. That is the form used downstream, e.g. `(↑(v.ideleFiniteCoord (unitEmbedding x)) : K_v) = algebraMap K K_v x`.
findings.proposed_change: State the RHS with the coerced hom, e.g. `Units.map (algebraMap K (v.adicCompletion K) : K →* v.adicCompletion K) x`, and likewise for `w.Completion`. This is the form simp already produces. Also add simp lemmas for the underlying coordinates: `((v.ideleFiniteCoord (IdeleGroup.unitEmbedding R K x) : (v.adicCompletion K)ˣ) : v.adicCompletion K) = algebraMap K (v.adicCompletion K) x`, and the analogue for `w.Completion`. Then the `Units.coe_map` / `toMonoidHom_eq_coe` / `coe_ofClass` cleanup in `ideleNorm_unitEmbedding` and the `rw [...]; simp` blocks in Congruence.lean and Kummer/Index.lean can be dropped.
findings.benefit: The simp set reaches a stable form in one step. The lemma is usable with `simp` and not only with `rw` followed by a manual `simp only` clean-up. Downstream proofs about principal ideles get shorter and no longer need the explicit list of normalisation lemmas.
